To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a new algorithm based on natural policy gradients and analyze the sample complexity for solving zero-sum Markov game in the tabular setting.

(i) we propose a new algorithmic framework for multi-agent reinforcement learning based on natural policy gradients and two time scale natural actor-critic; (ii) we provide a new analysis for the sample efficiency of our algorithm for solving zero-sum Markov Games, which is better than existing results for the same setting; (iii) we provide a numerical verification of our results on a two-player bandits problem and the two-player game Alesia; (iv) our algorithmic framework and sample complexity analysis
we introduce sample-efficient actor-critic based algorithms for zero-sum Markow games, with sample complexity that matches best-known results in the single agent case.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing efficient algorithms for multi-agent settings, with sample complexity matching the best-known results in the single agent case.
the sample efficiency of natural actor-critic algorithms and their application to zero-sum Markov game problems.
the following question: can we use the tools of single agent RL for multi-agent RL?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our work improves the best-known sample complexity results of policy gradient/ actor-critic methods in the multi-agent tabular setting, and also matches the best known results in the single agent tabular setting.

our work provides the first sample efficient algorithms for solving Markov games with a natural policy gradient and a two time-scale actor critic framework, and the first sample efficient actor-critic algorithms for solving zero-sum Markov Games.
we have improved sample complexities for policy gradient/actor critic based methods for solving two player Markov games.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first sample complexity analysis for natural actor-critic methods for solving Markov games.

we provide sample-efficient actor-critic based algorithms for multi-agent reinforcement learning, with sample complexities that are similar to the best known results in the single agent case, but with a requirement for agents to agree on etiquette.
we provide a new algorithmic framework to study multi-agent reinforcement learning problems and provide a sample-efficient algorithm to solve two player zero-sum tabular games.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sample complexity of actor-critic methods for solving Markov decision processes is not affected by the number of agents in the multi-agent system.
the sample complexity for solving Markov games is similar to the sample complexity for single agent RL.
, in the tabular setting, policy gradient methods can be used for solving zero-sum Markov game problems in a sample-efficient manner.
